paragraphs: Search rankings influence which results users notice and click, so user feedback can reflect presentation as well as relevance. This paper introduces Baidu-ULTR, a dataset intended to support research on learning rankings from such biased feedback. It addresses three shortcomings of existing benchmarks: missing original text, incomplete information about result presentation, and heavy reliance on simulated user behavior.

The dataset contains 1.2 billion randomly sampled search sessions and expert annotations for 7,008 queries, covering 397,572 query-document pairs. It supplies original semantic information and pretrained language models of different sizes. Researchers can therefore study text representations alongside the ranking problem, rather than relying entirely on previously extracted features.

Its display information includes result position, displayed height, and displayed abstracts. Recorded user behavior includes dwelling time, supporting investigation of engagement beyond clicks. The paper also presents dataset design principles and evaluates representative ranking algorithms. Its central contribution is a large empirical resource for studying several interacting sources of bias using real search feedback.
neurips-2022-a-large-scale-search-datase.tldr: Baidu-ULTR provides billion-scale search feedback, original text, and display information for studying unbiased learning to rank.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks learn solutions while being penalized for violating physical equations. Computing the spatial derivatives in these penalties through automatic differentiation can be expensive, especially for higher derivatives. This paper introduces discretely trained PINNs, which replace those spatial derivative calculations with accurate numerical approximations.

The method uses radial basis function finite differences to construct derivative approximations that can be applied through sparse matrix-vector multiplication. Because this technique is meshless, it also supports point samples on irregular geometries. The authors examine differentiation in networks with random weights and find that approximations of third-order accuracy or higher offer sufficient accuracy with greater efficiency in their experiments.

On linear and nonlinear Poisson equations, the proposed networks reach similar losses with training times reduced by a factor of two to four on a consumer GPU. These comparisons use 64-bit arithmetic for the proposed method and 32-bit arithmetic for conventional PINNs. Heat-equation experiments also support combining numerical spatial derivatives with automatic temporal differentiation. The findings show how scientific computing techniques can improve the measured balance between training cost and accuracy.
neurips-2022-accelerated-training-of-phy.tldr: Replacing automatic spatial differentiation with meshless numerical approximations accelerates PINN training while preserving comparable accuracy in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper studies discovery as a sequence of choices from a large collection of unlabeled candidates. Each selected point is labeled, revealing a response, and the objective is to maximize the total responses collected. This formulation captures settings where evaluating candidates serves an immediate discovery goal, as in searching for useful chemical reaction conditions.

The central difficulty is balancing information gathering against exploiting current predictions. A candidate can be valuable because its response is expected to be high, or because observing it improves estimates that guide later selections. Focusing entirely on either consideration can overlook the other source of value. The authors formalize this problem as Adaptive Sampling for Discovery.

They propose a general information-directed sampling algorithm and establish performance guarantees for linear, graph, and low-rank models. Simulations and experiments using real chemical reaction data demonstrate benefits of the approach. Together, the formulation and results connect model learning directly to cumulative discovery outcomes: the algorithm must account for what a measurement teaches as well as what it yields.
neurips-2022-adaptive-sampling-for-disco.tldr: Information-directed sampling balances learning about candidates with selecting promising ones to improve cumulative discovery outcomes.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether negative-free contrastive learning produces representations that separate the underlying factors of data. Such separation is called disentanglement. Although these methods have performed well in large-scale pretraining, the authors identify disentanglement as a property that had received little investigation in this setting.

Measurement is a central part of the contribution. The authors find that existing disentanglement metrics do not provide meaningful assessments for high-dimensional representations. They introduce a metric based on mutual information between learned representations and data factors, using statistical dependence to examine how those factors are reflected in the representation.

Using this metric, the study benchmarks negative-free contrastive methods on synthetic datasets and the real-world CelebA dataset. The investigated methods can learn a well-disentangled subset of their representations. That finding concerns a subset rather than establishing that every representation component cleanly separates data factors. The work therefore contributes both an evaluation approach for high-dimensional representations and empirical evidence about the structure learned by these pretraining methods.
neurips-2022-an-empirical-study-on-disen.tldr: A mutual-information-based evaluation finds well-disentangled representation subsets in the negative-free contrastive methods studied.

paragraphs: Learning functions with many output dimensions can require expensive training examples, such as results from numerical simulations. Multi-fidelity active learning chooses both where to collect an example and which fidelity to use. This paper extends that decision to batches, seeking informative collections of examples whose combined cost stays within a specified budget.

The motivation is that individually selected queries can be strongly correlated and provide overlapping information. BMFAL-BC evaluates a batch through its mutual information with the target function. This joint criterion discourages redundant queries and favors diversity, making the value of one query depend on what the other queries already contribute.

Choosing inputs and fidelities together creates a difficult combinatorial optimization problem. The authors develop a weighted greedy algorithm that builds the batch one fidelity-input pair at a time and achieves a near 1 − 1/e approximation to the optimum. Experiments in computational physics and engineering show advantages of the method. The contribution combines budget control with explicit attention to information overlap, improving how a batch uses costly evaluations.
neurips-2022-batch-multi-fidelity-active.tldr: BMFAL-BC selects diverse batches of queries across fidelities while respecting a total acquisition budget.

paragraphs: Models that fit their training data perfectly can still perform reasonably well on new data, even when training labels contain noise. This paper argues that explaining this behavior requires more than a distinction between harmless and disastrous overfitting. It introduces an intermediate category called tempered overfitting.

The three categories describe different limiting behaviors of prediction risk. In benign overfitting, performance approaches the Bayes-optimal level despite noise. In catastrophic overfitting, risk becomes unbounded. Tempered overfitting lies between them: the influence of noise remains bounded but still causes a persistent performance penalty. The authors argue that this middle category better captures the noisy-data behavior of practical interpolating models such as deep networks.

The paper supplies broad empirical evidence for this taxonomy across neural networks and kernel methods. It then derives conditions involving regularization and the kernel eigenspectrum that produce each behavior in kernel ridge regression. Experiments with natural and synthetic data illustrate consequences for common kernels and infinite-width trained neural networks. The resulting framework distinguishes tolerable noise sensitivity from genuinely optimal generalization.
neurips-2022-benign-tempered-or-catastro.tldr: Tempered overfitting describes models whose fitting of noisy data causes bounded but persistent generalization error.

paragraphs: Decentralized learning lets agents coordinate through peer-to-peer messages without a central server. Communicating with fewer neighbors can shorten each iteration, but information may then spread too slowly across the network. This paper addresses the tradeoff between local communication cost and the number of iterations needed to reach agreement.

The proposed EquiTopo family contains two designs. EquiStatic uses a number of neighbors that grows logarithmically with network size. EquiDyn uses time-varying connections generated through a particular random sampling procedure, with each agent communicating with one peer. Both designs achieve a consensus rate independent of network size, preserving efficient information mixing as the network grows.

The authors apply these topologies to decentralized stochastic gradient descent and decentralized gradient tracking. They report theoretical and empirical improvements in communication and convergence. The distinction between the designs matters: the static construction has slowly growing degree, whereas the dynamic construction has degree one. Their shared contribution is showing how sparse communication patterns can support effective network-wide coordination without requiring each agent to contact many others.
neurips-2022-communication-efficient-top.tldr: EquiTopo provides sparse communication patterns with network-size-independent consensus rates for decentralized learning.

paragraphs: Causal approaches to fairness use relationships between variables to reason about discrimination involving sensitive attributes. Many such methods assume that the complete causal graph is known. This paper develops a way to pursue counterfactual fairness when available evidence leaves some directions of causal influence unresolved.

The method works with a partially directed acyclic graph representing a class of possible causal graphs. Such a representation can be learned from observational data together with domain knowledge. The authors derive conditions and algorithms for identifying ancestral relationships between variables, then use those relationships to select features that lead to counterfactual fairness.

A specific result concerns background knowledge that sensitive attributes have no ancestors in the causal graph. When that knowledge is available, the authors show that counterfactual fairness can be achieved as if the true graph were fully known. This is a conditional result tied to the stated causal information. Experiments on simulated and real datasets demonstrate the method's effectiveness, supporting the use of partial causal knowledge in fair feature selection.
neurips-2022-counterfactual-fairness-wit.tldr: The paper derives fair feature-selection methods from partially known causal graphs, with a stronger result under specific knowledge about sensitive attributes.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation compresses training information into a small representation that can support later learning. This paper proposes HaBa, which represents distilled data through two reusable components: bases and image-producing networks called hallucination networks. Feeding bases into those networks reconstructs training images.

The approach shifts attention from storing representative images individually to learning components that can be combined flexibly. These combinations increase the representational capacity of the compressed dataset. HaBa is presented as a plug-and-play strategy for existing distillation methods. The authors also introduce paired adversarial contrastive constraints designed to increase generated-image diversity and strengthen information useful for distinguishing classes.

Experiments report substantial improvements in downstream classification compared with previous methods while reducing compressed parameter counts by up to 65%. The distilled data also achieve approximately 10% higher accuracy than baselines in cross-architecture generalization. These results support factorization as a way to make compressed training information more useful, including when the architecture consuming the distilled data differs from the one involved in producing it.
neurips-2022-dataset-distillation-via-fa.tldr: HaBa factorizes distilled datasets into reusable bases and image-generating networks, improving reported classification performance with fewer compressed parameters.

paragraphs: An agent learning an unknown environment must explore to improve its decisions, but exploration can conflict with safety requirements. This paper studies that problem in a finite-horizon constrained Markov decision process with unknown transition probabilities. Safety is expressed as bounds on expected cumulative costs that must hold in every learning episode.

The proposed model-based algorithm, DOPE, combines three ingredients. It uses standard optimistic model-based exploration, adds a reward bonus that encourages exploration, and imposes a conservative constraint to account for safety. The reward and constraint treatments play different roles: one encourages potentially useful actions, while the other restricts choices that could breach the modeled cost requirement.

The authors prove an objective regret bound of order |S|√(|A|K), up to logarithmic factors, while maintaining the safety constraints during learning. Here, |S| counts states, |A| counts actions, and K counts episodes. The safety statement concerns expected cumulative costs, as defined in the formulation. Experiments also show significant improvements over earlier optimism-pessimism approaches, complementing the stronger regret guarantee.
neurips-2022-dope-doubly-optimistic-and-.tldr: DOPE combines optimistic exploration with conservative cost constraints to improve regret while satisfying expected-cost safety requirements during learning.

paragraphs: Cooperating reinforcement-learning agents can use messages from teammates to coordinate their actions. Simply passing raw messages alongside local observations to a policy, however, leaves that policy to work out how the messages fit together. This paper proposes MASIA to organize incoming communication into compact information useful for decisions.

A message encoder aggregates the received messages into a shared representation. It is permutation invariant, so changing the order of the messages does not change the aggregation. The encoder learns through self-supervised objectives involving reconstruction and future information. A separate extraction mechanism then lets each agent select the portions of the aggregated representation most relevant to its own decision.

This separates the task of combining team information from the task of using that information locally. The authors report significant performance improvements over strong baselines across multiple cooperative tasks and task settings. The findings support the value of learning how to summarize and select communicated information, alongside learning the policies that ultimately choose actions.
neurips-2022-efficient-multi-agent-commu.tldr: MASIA learns compact summaries of teammate messages and lets each agent extract the information most relevant to its decisions.

paragraphs: A neural network trained to minimize errors on its training examples can lose accuracy when the test distribution changes. Invariant learning addresses this problem by seeking causal features that remain useful across distributional changes. This paper introduces EDNIL, a framework intended to make that kind of learning less dependent on prior information about the training environments.

EDNIL uses a neural network with multiple heads to absorb data biases. Within the framework, this provides a way to handle variation associated with the data while pursuing features that remain stable. The authors show that their approach does not require prior knowledge of environments or strong assumptions about a pretrained model, removing requirements that could complicate its use.

The paper also establishes theoretical connections to research on the properties of variant and invariant features. Its empirical results show greater robustness to distribution shifts for models trained with EDNIL. These findings support the framework's approach to managing bias during invariant learning; the reported robustness is an experimental result rather than a claim that performance remains unchanged under every possible shift.
neurips-2022-environment-diversification.tldr: EDNIL uses a multi-head network to absorb data biases and empirically improves distribution-shift robustness without prior environment knowledge.

paragraphs: This paper develops a deterministic method for globally optimizing K-medoids clustering. Its branch-and-bound procedure explores possible solutions while using lower bounds to determine which search regions can be discarded. The aim is to accompany a clustering solution with evidence about its distance from the best possible objective value.

The key component is a tailored Lagrangian relaxation that supplies a lower bound at each search node and a guaranteed maximum gap at the root. The bound has an analytical closed-form solution, avoiding a separate optimization problem for its computation, and can be evaluated in parallel. Additional bound-tightening techniques shrink the search space and reduce computational work.

The authors prove finite convergence to a global optimum while branching only on medoid regions. Computational studies cover 28 datasets and report solutions certified to a 0.1% optimality gap within four hours for datasets containing up to one million samples. Their objective values match or improve on the compared heuristic. The convergence theorem and finite-tolerance experiments together address both correctness and practical scale.
neurips-2022-global-optimal-k-medoids-cl.tldr: A branch-and-bound method scales certified K-medoids optimization to tested datasets with up to one million samples.

paragraphs: Online learners can benefit when observations contain little noise, but the noise variances may be unknown beforehand. This paper develops sharper regret analyses for variance-adaptive linear bandits and linear mixture Markov decision processes. Regret measures the accumulated performance loss associated with learning rather than already having the best decisions available.

For linear bandits, the bound is the smaller of d√K and d^1.5√(Σσ²), plus d², with logarithmic factors suppressed. Here d is feature dimension, K is the number of steps, and Σσ² is cumulative noise variance. The variance-dependent term captures potential benefits from lower noise without requiring advance knowledge of those variances. The authors report a factor-d³ improvement over the preceding analysis.

For linear mixture processes, the regret bound becomes d√K + d², again suppressing logarithmic factors. This horizon-free result assumes that maximum cumulative reward per episode lies in [0,1]; d counts base models and K counts episodes. A new peeling-based analysis using an elliptical potential count lemma drives the improvements, sharpening guarantees in both settings.
neurips-2022-improved-regret-analysis-fo.tldr: New analyses substantially tighten variance-adaptive linear-bandit regret bounds and horizon-free bounds for normalized-reward linear mixture processes.

paragraphs: N:M sparsity constrains each group of M consecutive network weights to contain N nonzero weights. This structure can combine strong predictive performance with acceleration on NVIDIA A100 GPUs, but existing training approaches can require pretraining or expensive training from scratch. This paper proposes learning the sparse structure during ordinary training.

The method, called Learning Best Combination, treats each group as a choice among all possible combinations of N retained weights. Every candidate combination receives a learnable importance score that is optimized jointly with its weights. The authors prove that the magnitude of an optimized score reflects the corresponding combination's importance to the training loss.

Training progressively removes combinations with smaller scores until one remains. This connects the final sparsity pattern to learned combination-level importance and avoids a separate pretraining phase. Across the networks and datasets examined, the method consistently improves the efficacy of existing N:M approaches. Its main contribution is making structured sparsity a selection process embedded in training, with theoretical support for the scores used to make those selections.
neurips-2022-learning-best-combination-f.tldr: LBC learns scores for candidate weight combinations and progressively selects an N:M sparse pattern during training from scratch.

paragraphs: This paper proposes Hat EBM, a way to build an energy-based probabilistic model around a generator network. The formulation treats an observed image as the sum of a generator output and a residual random variable. That residual accounts for the gap between what the generator produces and the image being modeled.

The generator becomes part of the energy model's forward computation. Training does not require recovering the latent variables associated with observed images, nor does it require calculating the generator's Jacobian determinant. These properties allow the approach to incorporate different types of generator networks, including generators that were not themselves constructed as probabilistic models.

Experiments demonstrate strong performance in unconditional ImageNet synthesis at 128 by 128 resolution, refinement of existing generator outputs, and energy-based modeling with non-probabilistic generators. These tasks illustrate complementary uses of the same formulation: producing images, improving a generator's outputs, and adding explicit probabilistic modeling around an existing generator. The residual component is central because the modeled image need not coincide exactly with a generator output.
neurips-2022-learning-probabilistic-mode.tldr: Hat EBM combines a generator with a residual variable to enable energy-based probabilistic modeling without latent inference or generator Jacobian determinants.

paragraphs: Training a decision tree requires repeatedly choosing where to split the data. This paper introduces MABSplit, a splitting procedure designed to accelerate random forests and related tree-based methods. It uses ideas from multi-armed bandits to decide how samples and computation should be distributed among candidate split points.

The central idea is to allocate evaluation effort selectively while searching for a split. The authors provide theoretical guarantees improving the sample complexity of each node split from linear to logarithmic in the number of data points. This targets a repeated operation inside tree construction, allowing improvements at individual nodes to affect overall forest training.

In some tested settings, MABSplit reduces training time by a factor of 100 without reducing generalization performance. Similar speedups appear in variants including Extremely Random Forests and Random Patches, and the method supports classification and regression. Under a fixed computational budget, it also outperforms existing methods in predictive generalization and feature-importance calculations. The reported gains demonstrate both faster training and better use of a limited compute budget.
neurips-2022-mabsplit-faster-forest-trai.tldr: MABSplit adaptively allocates split-evaluation effort, achieving up to 100-fold forest-training speedups in some tested settings.

paragraphs: Backdoor poisoning inserts triggers into some training examples so that a model learns an attacker-chosen prediction when those triggers appear. This paper investigates whether controlling the adaptation of pretrained language models can reduce that vulnerability while retaining useful performance on the intended task.

The motivation is an observed two-stage learning pattern on poisoned data. During moderate fitting, models primarily learn the major task features. During later overfitting, they also learn the subsidiary features associated with backdoor triggers. The proposed defense aims to keep adaptation within the earlier stage. The authors design three strategies that respectively reduce model capacity, the number of training epochs, and the learning rate.

Experiments show that these strategies defend effectively against several representative language-model backdoor attacks. Visualization analyses examine how different features are learned, and additional investigations consider poisoning ratios and possible application to pretrained vision models. The central claim is conditional on properly restricting adaptation: the observed learning order creates an opportunity to preserve task learning while reducing the acquisition of trigger behavior.
neurips-2022-moderate-fitting-as-a-natur.tldr: Restricting pretrained language-model adaptation to moderate fitting helps resist tested backdoor attacks while retaining useful task performance.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a moving scene requires estimating both its shape and how that shape changes over time. Neural-DynamicReconstruction, or NDR, addresses this using color and depth observations from a single RGB-D camera. It does not require a predefined shape template and seeks to recover detailed geometry together with scene motion.

NDR represents the surface with a neural implicit function and jointly optimizes the surface and its deformations using captured color and depth. An invertible neural deformation network constrains non-rigid motion. Its construction automatically satisfies cycle consistency between arbitrary pairs of frames, keeping the deformation mappings mutually consistent.

The method also accounts for changes in surface topology over time through a topology-aware correspondence strategy for frames being fused. Global optimization further refines camera poses, so camera estimation participates in the overall reconstruction. Experiments on public datasets and a dataset collected by the authors outperform existing monocular dynamic reconstruction methods. The approach brings surface shape, deformation, correspondence, and camera refinement into a coordinated reconstruction process.
neurips-2022-neural-surface-reconstructi.tldr: NDR jointly reconstructs dynamic surfaces and motion from one RGB-D camera using consistent deformation mappings and topology-aware correspondences.

paragraphs: Pretrained vision models are adapted to many downstream tasks, raising the question of whether an attack prepared before adaptation can remain effective afterward. This paper introduces pretrained adversarial perturbations, or PAPs: universal perturbations crafted using a pretrained model without knowledge of the downstream tasks they will later target.

The proposed Low-Level Layer Lifting Attack generates these perturbations by increasing neuron activations in the pretrained model's lower layers. It also uses an enhanced noise augmentation strategy to improve transfer to fine-tuned models. The intended transfer is therefore across adaptation: the attack is constructed against the shared pretrained starting point and evaluated against models derived from it.

Experiments cover typical pretrained vision models and ten downstream tasks. The authors report a large improvement in attack success rate over existing methods. This provides empirical evidence that perturbations can retain effectiveness through fine-tuning even when downstream-task information is unavailable during attack construction. The contribution highlights robustness of pretrained representations as relevant to the security of their later adaptations.
neurips-2022-pre-trained-adversarial-per.tldr: PAPs exploit pretrained models to create perturbations that transfer effectively to tested fine-tuned models without downstream-task knowledge.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns categories across an image, making spatial context central to accurate predictions. This paper introduces SegNeXt, a convolutional architecture that revisits how attention can encode that context. The authors examine characteristics of successful segmentation models and use those findings to design attention around inexpensive convolutional operations.

The design tests whether convolutional attention can provide a more effective and efficient way to capture context than transformer self-attention. SegNeXt reports substantial improvements over previous leading methods on benchmarks including ADE20K, Cityscapes, COCO-Stuff, Pascal VOC, Pascal Context, and iSAID. These comparisons connect the architectural argument to segmentation performance across several datasets.

On the Pascal VOC 2012 test leaderboard, SegNeXt reaches 90.6% mean intersection over union while using one tenth the parameters of EfficientNet-L2 with NAS-FPN, which it outperforms. On ADE20K, the authors report average improvements of about 2.0% mIoU with equal or lower computation. The results support convolutional attention as a competitive way to combine contextual modeling with computational efficiency in the evaluated segmentation settings.
neurips-2022-segnext-rethinking-convolut.tldr: SegNeXt uses inexpensive convolutional attention to improve segmentation accuracy and efficiency across the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Contextual bandit algorithms must balance trying uncertain actions with choosing actions that currently appear best. Hyperparameters control this balance and other aspects of behavior. This paper addresses tuning those parameters during interaction, where decisions must be made in real time and no pre-collected dataset is available for conventional offline tuning.

The authors first introduce a two-layer bandit structure for automatically adjusting an exploration parameter. They then generalize the idea into Syndicated Bandits, a framework that dynamically learns multiple hyperparameters. The framework applies to several widely used contextual bandit algorithms, including LinUCB, LinTS, and UCB-GLM, making tuning part of the ongoing learning process.

The analysis derives regret bounds that avoid exponential dependence on the number of tuned hyperparameters. Optimal regret is achieved in certain scenarios, rather than claimed for every application of the framework. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets validate its effectiveness. The contribution is a general approach to adapting the settings of an online learner while controlling the performance cost of that adaptation.
neurips-2022-syndicated-bandits-a-framew.tldr: Syndicated Bandits tunes contextual-bandit hyperparameters online with regret guarantees that avoid exponential dependence on the number of parameters.

paragraphs: Hyperdimensional computing uses high-dimensional binary vectors and is attractive for energy-efficient, low-latency hardware. Its predictive accuracy, however, has been limited, with little theoretical explanation of the restriction. This paper studies that restriction through the similarity relationships that binary vector representations can express.

The authors characterize representable similarity matrices and show how random Fourier features can approach the limits of binary hyperdimensional computing. They then broaden the analysis to vector symbolic architectures, whose high-dimensional vectors need not be binary. Within this broader family, they introduce finite group architectures that can surpass the representational limits of the binary approach.

Representation theory is used both to characterize the similarity matrices available to these finite group architectures and to show how to construct them. Experiments find that the random Fourier feature method and the group-based architecture can outperform the compared leading HDC model by up to 7.6% while retaining hardware efficiency. The work connects accuracy limits to representational choices and supplies constructions that improve performance within or beyond those limits.
neurips-2022-understanding-hyperdimensio.tldr: The paper explains representational limits of binary hyperdimensional computing and develops hardware-efficient approaches with improved reported accuracy.

paragraphs: Vision-language pretraining can learn from relationships between images and text, while additional self-supervision can exploit relationships among images. This paper argues that defining these contrastive objectives in separate spaces overlooks useful combinations of supervision. UniCLIP brings cross-domain and within-domain pairs into one universal contrastive space.

Combining these pair types creates discrepancies because their domains and relationships differ. UniCLIP addresses this with three components: augmentation-aware feature embeddings, an MP-NCE loss, and a domain-dependent similarity measure. Together, they support the shared training objective while accounting for distinctions among the kinds of pairs being compared.

The authors evaluate UniCLIP on downstream tasks involving a single modality as well as multiple modalities and report improvements over previous vision-language pretraining methods. Their experiments also show that each proposed component contributes to final performance. The findings support coordinating multiple sources of contrastive supervision within a common framework, with explicit mechanisms for their differences, as a useful way to improve the representations learned during pretraining.
neurips-2022-uniclip-unified-framework-f.tldr: UniCLIP unifies image-text and within-domain contrastive supervision, improving performance on the evaluated downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Adversarial training can be supplemented with unlabeled real or generated examples that receive predicted labels. This paper investigates why artificially generated examples can improve robustness in that framework. Its statistical analysis focuses on two interacting factors: the strength of the adversarial attack and the quality of the unlabeled-data generator.

The results show that a high-quality generator can provide substantial benefits when attack strength is large. A poor generator can still help to some extent, so the analysis does not reduce the value of generated data to a simple useful-or-useless distinction. Instead, the expected contribution depends on the quality of the supplementary data and the adversarial training conditions.

The authors use these insights to propose an algorithm that adjusts the relative weights of labeled real data and generated data during training. The adjustment aims to optimize adversarial risk while accounting for generated-data quality. Numerical studies support the theoretical results and demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness. The work therefore combines an explanation of synthetic-data benefits with a practical mechanism for adapting how strongly training relies on them.
neurips-2022-why-do-artificially-generat.tldr: The paper links synthetic-data benefits to generator quality and attack strength, then adaptively weights generated and real data during adversarial training.
